summary: A provider-agnostic AI chat panel. Keen renders the conversation, streams the assistant reply, and owns keyboard, focus, and screen-reader behavior. The host connects its AI provider through an adapter and keeps the conversation.

design.note: The .pen file is a visual review artifact, not a token source. Its variables are generated from the DTCG tokens by pnpm design:push and named after tier token paths. Pen 0.3 cannot bind width or height to a variable, so chat.message-max-width and chat.composer-height are applied as numbers and named in those layers' metadata. The rate-limit notice names chat.composer-height as its minimum height in metadata and otherwise fits its content. The user bubble's chat.message-max-width binding is an implementation decision; the design's user bubble carries no width metadata.

host: Conversation lifecycle: when a chat starts, resets, or is discarded
Rate limits and connectivity: whether a limit applies, its retry time, and whether the user is online
Product copy passed through labels and slots

states.name: empty
states.description: No messages yet. The empty slot and optional suggestions fill the log.

states.name: loading
states.description: The request is sent and no text has arrived. A pending message shows the thinking label.
states.announcement: The live region says the thinking label once.

states.name: streaming
states.description: Text chunks append to the assistant message, which is marked busy.
states.announcement: Only newly appended text is announced, flushed at sentence ends.

states.name: completed
states.description: The adapter finished. The full response is in the log.
states.announcement: Any unannounced remainder is flushed. The full message is not re-read.

states.name: error
states.description: The adapter failed before any text arrived. An error notice with Retry follows the user message.
states.announcement: The error notice is a role=alert region, announced once.

states.name: stopped
states.description: The user stopped generation. The partial response stays and shows the stopped status.
states.announcement: The live region says the stopped label.

states.name: error-mid-stream
states.description: The adapter failed after text arrived. The partial response stays and an error notice with Retry follows it.
states.announcement: The error notice is a role=alert region, announced once.

states.name: rate-limited
states.description: The host reported a rate limit. A notice with a countdown to the retry time, or a fallback detail without one, replaces the input. The log is unchanged.
states.announcement: The notice is a polite role=status region, announced once with the retry time. Countdown ticks are not announced.

states.name: offline
states.description: The host reports no connection. A banner shows below the header and Send is disabled; the input still takes a draft. The log is unchanged.
states.announcement: The banner is a polite role=status region, announced once. The live region says the back-online label on reconnect.

transitions.event: retry: drop the partial, resend the same request
host sets a rateLimit that applies, or a limit applies when this state is entered
retryAt passes or host sets rateLimit to null
host sets online to false, or online is still false when this state is entered

anatomy.description: The panel. Fills the box the host gives it.
Shows labels.title, or the header slot.
Icon, title, and detail. Shown below the header while online is false.
Scrollable conversation. One li per message, notice, or pending reply.
User text in an end-aligned bubble.
Assistant text in a start-aligned bubble, plus a status line when stopped.
Error title, detail, and the Retry button.
Default icon, title, and body, or the empty slot.
One per suggestions entry, below the empty content. Sends its text.
Message input and the Send or Stop action.
Message input with a visually hidden label.
Icon button. Disabled while the input is empty; aria-disabled while offline.
Replaces Send while loading or streaming.
Icon, title, and the countdown or fallback detail. Replaces the input and Send while rate limited; the composer keeps its padding and divider.
Visually hidden. Carries loading, streaming, stopped, back-online, and limit-lifted announcements.

types: interface ChatMessage { id: string; role: ChatRole; content: string; status?: "complete" | "stopped" | "error"; }
interface ChatAdapter { send(request: ChatRequest, signal: AbortSignal): AsyncIterable<string>; }

props.name: adapter
props.description: Host connection to the AI provider. send yields text chunks, throws on failure, and should stop when signal aborts.

props.name: initialMessages
props.description: Conversation to restore on mount. An empty list starts in the empty state.

props.name: onMessagesChange
props.description: Called with the full list whenever a message is added, removed, or reaches a terminal status, including when Retry drops a partial response. Not called per chunk. The host persists from here.

props.name: onError
props.description: Called with the adapter error on entering error or error-mid-stream.

props.name: labels
props.description: All visible and announced copy. ChatLabels has one string per key in api.labels; omitted keys use those English defaults.

props.name: suggestions
props.description: Prompts shown in the empty state. Activating one sends its text.

props.name: online
props.description: Host connectivity signal, for example from navigator.onLine and the online and offline events. While false, the chat is offline.

props.name: rateLimit
props.description: Set by the host when its server reports a limit. While a limit applies, the chat is rate limited. retryAt is when sending is allowed again and enables the countdown.

props.name: header
props.description: Slot. Replaces the default header content. The region keeps labels.title as its name.

props.name: empty
props.description: Slot. Replaces the default empty-state icon, title, and body. Suggestions still render below it.

labels.title: Assistant
labels.interruptedDetail: The partial reply above is kept. Retry replaces it.
labels.emptyBody: Ask a question to get started.
labels.rateLimitDetail: Try again in a little while.
labels.offlineDetail: Your draft is kept. Send works again when you reconnect.

behavior: Submitting trims the input, appends a user message, clears the input, and calls adapter.send with the conversation.
Stop aborts the signal and ignores any later chunks; an abort rejection after Stop is not an error.
Stopping before any text keeps no assistant bubble; the stopped status line still shows.
Retry after error-mid-stream removes the partial assistant message before resending.
To reset a conversation, the host remounts Chat with a new key and initialMessages.
online and rateLimit are host signals. Keen never detects connectivity or limits and never reconnects or retries on its own; a request that fails goes to error or error-mid-stream as usual.
While online is false, the input still takes a draft, but Enter, Send, Retry, and suggestions do not send. When online turns true, the banner goes and the live region says labels.backOnline.

A limit applies while rateLimit is set and its retryAt, if any, has not passed. Once retryAt passes, the limit no longer applies even if the host leaves rateLimit set, until the host passes a new rateLimit. While a limit applies, the rate-limit notice replaces the input and the draft is kept for when the input returns. Enter, Send, Retry, and suggestions do not send. With retryAt, the notice shows labels.rateLimitCountdown with {time} as the remaining m:ss; without it, labels.rateLimitDetail.
The input returns when retryAt passes or the host sets rateLimit to null, whichever is first, and the live region says labels.rateLimitLifted.

Each signal is tracked on its own: the banner shows while online is false and the notice replaces the input while a limit applies, whichever state is active, so both can apply at once. Neither signal changes the log, so leaving rate-limited or offline returns to the state it interrupted, and the other state follows at once only if online is still false or a limit still applies. If both apply when a state is entered, rate-limited is entered.

Set during loading or streaming, neither signal interrupts the reply: the banner shows at once with Stop still available, and the notice waits for the reply to end. When the reply ends, the chat enters rate-limited if a limit applies, or offline if online is still false. A host that learns of a limit from a failed send can set rateLimit from onError; the error notice stays, with Retry disabled until the limit lifts.

overrides.note: With semantic tokens, these are the only supported customization surface. Chat has no variants in 0.2.0. It forwards no className or style to its internals, and internal selectors are not stable. A need these cannot meet becomes a reviewed Keen change.

structure: Root is a vertical stack: header, log, composer. It fills the host's box; the host sets size and placement.
The log takes the remaining height and scrolls. It follows new content while scrolled to the bottom and stays put when the user has scrolled up.
User bubbles align to the end, assistant bubbles to the start. Bubbles are at most chat.message-max-width wide and never wider than the log.
The empty state centers in the log. Suggestions stack below it.
An error notice spans the log width and follows the last message.
The offline banner sits between the header and the log at full panel width. It does not scroll with the log.
The rate-limit notice takes the place of the input and Send inside the composer's padding. It is at least chat.composer-height tall, so the log keeps its height.
The composer field is at least chat.composer-height tall. The input grows with its content to six lines, then scrolls.
Send and Stop occupy the same slot at the end of the field; only one renders at a time.

keyboard.where: input with text, not loading, streaming, or offline

keyboard.action: Commits the composition; does not send.

keyboard.where: input or Stop, loading or streaming

keyboard.action: Activates the button. Does nothing while it is aria-disabled by offline or a rate limit.
Follows DOM order: header content, log, Retry, suggestions, input, Send or Stop.

focus: After a send from the input, Send, or a suggestion, focus is in the input.
When Stop or Retry disappears while focused, focus moves to the input.

When the rate-limit notice replaces the input while focus is in the composer, focus moves to the notice (tabindex -1). When the input returns and focus is still on the notice, focus moves to the input.
Controls disabled by offline or a rate limit use aria-disabled, not disabled, so they keep focus and stay in the tab order. Going offline or back online never moves focus.
Focus is never moved otherwise: streaming, completion, and errors do not steal focus.
The log is focusable (tabindex 0) so keyboard users can scroll it.
The input field shows a 2px color.semantic.focus ring while the input has focus; buttons show the same ring on focus-visible.
No focus trap and no autofocus on mount.
screenReader: The root is a region named by labels.title.
The log is a region named by labels.conversation. It is not a live region, so updates are not read twice.
Each message starts with a visually hidden speaker name: labels.userName or labels.assistantName.
The streaming message has aria-busy=true until it reaches a terminal state.
One polite live region announces the thinking label, then only newly appended text at sentence ends, then the stopped label when stopped.
Error notices use role=alert and are announced once.
The offline banner is a role=status region, announced once when it appears. On reconnect the live region says labels.backOnline.

The rate-limit notice is a role=status region, announced once when it appears. Its visible countdown is aria-hidden, so ticks are never announced; a visually hidden labels.rateLimitUntil gives retryAt as a clock time in the user's locale instead. When the limit lifts, the live region says labels.rateLimitLifted.
The input has a visually hidden label from labels.input. Send's accessible name is labels.send; Stop and Retry use their visible text.
Icons, dots, and the streaming caret are aria-hidden. Animations stop under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.
